summary: Okanogan NF summit in Okanogan County, WA; an L-5 cab built in 1934 and gone by 1953. WillhiteWeb's April 2020 visit found communication towers on the summit, and the register says a small ski lift is on the site now.

facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1953; WillhiteWeb found communication towers on the summit in April 2020, and the register says a small ski lift is on the site now
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Okanogan National Forest

access.note: Summer hiking route from the summer gate closure up the steep communication-tower access road. A lift can be used in winter. Access to the tower compound is not described.

visit.trail_note: 1.5 miles with about 1,300 feet of gain from the summer gate closure; a lift can be used in winter

events.note: Register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb all date the L-5 cab to 1934
Register says removed; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed
Newest communication tower installed in 2019/2020, per a WillhiteWeb photo caption

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in 1953, while firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say it was destroyed that year. All three place the loss in 1953.

sources.title: Little Buck Mtn. Fire Lookout Cabin

notes_for_editor: The 1934 build date and 1953 loss are consistent across all three sources. Today's condition rests on a WillhiteWeb visit in April 2020, not a current source. Access (summer gate closure, lift in winter) is per WillhiteWeb and not verified. The site is a communications site with towers; the story does not encourage climbing them. The register's ski lift photo caption is noted but not credited.
